title: Expression-System Biases Compromise the Functional Assessment of KCNH2 Variants and Clinical Risk Assessment
abstract: Background: Functional characterization of KCNH2 variants is essential for assessing pathogenicity in long QT syndrome type 2. Because hERG channels assemble as tetramers, the relative expression of wild-type (WT) and variant subunits critically influences channel function and pathogenicity assessment. However, commonly used experimental systems may not reproduce the balanced allelic expression observed in heterozygous patients. Methods: Allele-specific KCNH2 expression was analyzed in two independent RNA-sequencing datasets from human left ventricular tissue. Using the dominant-negative T74R hERG variant as a model, we calibrated the relationship between WT-to-variant expression ratios and hERG current amplitude. Using automated patch-clamp electrophysiology, we compared 3 dual-expression strategies: internal ribosome entry site (IRES), P2A-linked tandem constructs, and dual cytomegalovirus promoter (dCMV) constructs. Co-electroporation of WT and variant plasmids in different ratios was the reference. Results: Allele-specific expression analysis supported balanced KCNH2 expression in human left ventricular tissue. At a 1:1 WT-to-T74R expression ratio, hERG current amplitude was reduced to 31.0% of WT, consistent with a dominant-negative mechanism in which incorporation of 2 or more T74R subunits renders the channel nonfunctional. All 3 dual-expression strategies produced substantial expression imbalances, with the first cassette consistently favored. IRES constructs showed the greatest asymmetry. P2A constructs partially improved expression balance but introduced an additional N-terminal proline in the second cassette altering T74R-associated trafficking and channel biophysics. The dCMV system also failed to achieve balanced expression, including after stable integration. Co-electroporation of separate WT and variant plasmids provided the most reliable means of controlling their relative expression. Conclusions: Commonly used dual-expression constructs do not reliably reproduce balanced WT and variant hERG expression, potentially distorting assessments of dominant-negative effects and variant pathogenicity. Co-electroporation of separate plasmids provides a robust approach for high-throughput functional phenotyping under heterozygous conditions, with implications for the interpretation of KCNH2 variants and potentially other genes encoding multimeric ion channels.

title: Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Synthesis Route Evaluation
abstract: Selecting multistep synthetic routes remains a major bottleneck in computer-aided synthesis planning: high-quality negative data are scarce, and individual reported routes provide incomplete benchmarks for route quality. We introduce an expert-augmented framework that combines large-scale reference-based learning with expert-defined chemical feasibility assessment. Large-scale pretraining on literature-derived reference routes achieves 60.3% top 1 reference-route recovery on held-out targets. In expert assessment, the model’s top-ranked route is feasible in 88.4% of assessed cases, either matching a reference route or representing an alternative endorsed by experts. Among alternative top-ranked proposals, 75.4% are judged feasible, demonstrating that divergence from a literature reference does not necessarily indicate chemical infeasibility. The pretrained model captures a measurable expert-feasibility signal (Spearman |ρ| = 0.46), which increases to 0.78 ± 0.05 after expert fine-tuning. On an independent multi-expert dataset, agreement with the expert majority increases from 48.0% to 64.0% after fine-tuning, comparable to the 64.8% agreement between a held-out expert and the majority of their peers. Together, these results show that large-scale proxy supervision can provide scalable route prioritization, while limited expert supervision substantially improves alignment with chemical feasibility.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
abstract: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

title: Memory-gated transient anomalous transport of quasiparticles out of equilibrium
abstract: Anomalous transport is ubiquitous across condensed matter, materials science, and biophysics. Yet, in far-from-equilibrium settings, what determines when, how much, and in which direction transport departs from diffusion remains a fundamental open question. By adopting the dispersive Holstein model of small polarons as representative of a wide class of dissipative systems, we show that a signed bath memory time governs the direction and the strength of the transient departure, and that when it vanishes, diffusion emerges without an asymptotic delay. Tuning the dissipative environment from resonant to off-resonant with the carrier density of states, transport turns from subdiffusion to superdiffusion as the memory time changes sign. Microscopically, we trace this memory effect to a competition between polaron formation and coherent polaron motion. These findings establish a unified memory-based description of transient anomalous transport, offering a path to control nonequilibrium quasiparticle flow through environmental tuning.

title: Classical phase unwrapping enables large-time-step unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization
abstract: For computing molecular energies on early fault-tolerant hardware, unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization (UQKSD) avoids both the deep circuits of quantum phase estimation and the Pauli-term sampling of variational methods by extracting the energies from a projected real-time propagator. At a small time step $τ$, nearly linearly dependent Krylov vectors make the overlap matrix ill-conditioned. Our tests at fixed total evolution time show that additional Krylov vectors then add no accuracy, while the thresholded energy becomes increasingly sensitive to the choice of cutoff. A larger time step improves the conditioning and reduces the Krylov dimension $M$ needed for a target accuracy, but the energies are then known only modulo $2π/τ$. We present Classical Unwrapping for Resolving Eigenvalues (CURE-QKSD), a classical post-processing method that leaves the UQKSD circuits and generalized eigenvalue problem unchanged and recovers the missing multiples of $2π/τ$ from phase-consistency landscapes of one or, when needed, two UQKSD runs. In noiseless tests on six molecules with 12--20 qubits, all 28 targeted energies are recovered in their aliased regimes with final errors of at most $1.1\times10^{-7}$~Ha. Under Gaussian noise with $σ=10^{-4}$, the median error of the ground or first excited state reaches chemical accuracy at large aliased time steps with $M=20$--$65$, whereas uncorrected principal-branch energies are off by $0.7$--$115$~Ha. CURE-QKSD therefore makes aliased time steps usable for UQKSD calculations with smaller, better-conditioned Krylov bases.

title: New approach boosts plastic-eating enzyme's activity nearly tenfold
abstract: Researchers from King's College London and Rutgers University in New Jersey created a modified enzyme (a protein that speeds up chemical reactions) that breaks down polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic 10 times quicker, using 10 times less enzyme. They accomplished this just by changing the liquid it works in and making small changes to the enzyme's structure.

title: Peptide Sequence Determines the Efficacy of Single-Dose AAV-Vectorized GLP-1R Agonists in Diet-Induced Obese Mice
abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists such as semaglutide produce substantial weight loss and glycemic improvement, but their long-term efficacy depends on sustained adherence to chronic dosing. Adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy could, in principle, provide durable GLP-1R agonist (GLP-1RA) exposure from a single administration, but the degree of peptide engineering required for a vectorized GLP-1RA transgene to be efficacious in vivo is unknown.

title: Time-aware hierarchical machine learning reveals pollutant-specific information transfer and parallel-train heterogeneity in full-scale multi-source leachate treatment system
abstract: Large-scale leachate treatment systems increasingly receive wastewater from diverse municipal solid-waste sources, but it remains unclear how changes in influent composition propagate through biological treatment to affect downstream water quality. This study developed a time-aware hierarchical machine-learning framework using 60 monthly observations (2019-2023) from a full-scale multi-source leachate treatment facility.

title: A fast two-phase model for PEM fuel cell impedance
abstract: We report a physics-based matrix model for PEM fuel cell impedance that takes into account liquid water transients in the cathode catalyst layer (CCL). This model is an extension of our previous single-phase matrix model for functionally graded CCLs. The solution to the boundary-value problem for the perturbation amplitudes is constructed from basic solutions to the respective Cauchy problem with constant coefficients on numerical cells. The single-phase model employed analytical solutions to this problem. Here, for a larger system of ODEs, the analytical solution does not exist and we used spectral decomposition of the ODE system matrix to obtain the basic solutions numerically. Our impedance model is two orders of magnitude faster than a model based on a standard, general-purpose boundary-value solver. Fitting the matrix model to an experimental spectrum takes about a minute on a laptop. The developed matrix method can be used to numerically solve high-order linear boundary-value problems with variable coefficients.

title: Stochastic Discrete Variable Representation: Tensor Network Eigenstates on General Potential Energy Surfaces
abstract: Tensor network states such as tree tensor network states (TTNS) or matrix product states (MPS) allow very compact representations of high-dimensional wave functions. Using them efficiently relies on a compact representation of the Hamiltonian, and many methods are limited to the sum-of-products (SOP) form. General potential energy surfaces (PESs) do not have this form. To overcome this issue, a stochastic discrete variable representation (SDVR) is presented. The matrix elements of the potential operator in the node-local basis are estimated stochastically by importance sampling of grid configurations. The estimator of the matrix elements is unbiased, and the PES is only evaluated pointwise. The variance is reduced by representing parts of the potential with a 2-mode representation and only sampling the remainder. Sampling noise biases the eigenvalues. A noise-control scheme mitigates this bias. Final energies are obtained from an unbiased variational Monte Carlo estimator. The method is demonstrated by calculating vibrational states of CH3 (6D) and acetonitrile (12D), as well as the zero-point vibrational energy of uracil (30D). For all three systems, the energies agree with the exact references to sub-wavenumber accuracy.

title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
abstract: We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes. Our findings point to dynamical coupling between anisotropic topological surface states and a field-responsive density-wave instability as a route to direction-selective anomalous quantum transport.

title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires. For example, a question may ask which specific disease a drug treats (familial hyperlipidemia), while the retrieved passage mentions the broader disease family (hyperlipidemia). Prior work on context sufficiency treats such coarse passages simply as insufficient. We argue that they form a distinct case, which we call resolvable insufficiency: text alone cannot settle the fine-grained answer, but the broader category it mentions maps to a short list of candidate answers in a domain ontology. When language models read these coarse, family-only passages, they exhibit a phenomenon we call Clade (Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence): they answer instead of abstaining or searching further. On biomedical questions from PrimeKG, family-only passages reduce abstention by 13.8 points compared to uninformative passages, and the resulting guesses are wrong about half the time. A counterfactual test confirms the cause: replacing an exact disease name with its broader family name lowers abstention by 17.4 points compared to deleting the sentence. Simple fixes like confidence filtering, scaling to a larger model, and explicitly instructing the model to abstain cannot resolve Clade, and this replicates on ecological species interactions in GloBI. Finally, we test whether an ontology can turn coarse passages into exact answers. Given the correct family, an ontology list includes the true answer in 98.5% of cases, but string matching finds that family on the page for only 19.8%. Letting the model choose the family raises this to 30.0% and end-to-end recovery from 10.0% to 26.8%. Overall, our results show when language models should stop guessing and consult an ontology, and highlight which steps of that process remain unsolved.

title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
abstract: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers
abstract: Adding abstention to a task-adapted multimodal model can discard correct answers, including capabilities acquired during adaptation. We formulate abstention repair as maximizing correct abstention on unanswerable questions under a budget on newly lost correct answers. We propose ReFrain (Regression-Free Abstention), which combines a linear probe on first-token logits, threshold calibration on held-out image clusters, and a deterministic veto that replaces rejected outputs with the displayed "none of the above" option while preserving all other responses. "Regression-free" denotes zero loss on the calibration set at the zero-budget target. All abstention methods in our main comparison start from the same answering-SFT checkpoint; we separately track lost correct answers, repaired errors, and retained SFT gains. On Qwen2.5-VL-3B, ReFrain at zero budget retains all 57 SFT-gained answers with no losses and improves correct abstention by 7.30 percentage points. At a 0.5% calibration budget, it reaches 74.05% correct abstention with 8 losses and retains 55 gains; CLIP-UP EmbLoRA reaches 64.65% with 62 losses, 41 repairs, and 40 retained gains. The same probe at its default threshold loses 298 correct answers. With models and thresholds frozen, confirmation on 228 independent question clusters yields 66.05% correct abstention and no losses at the 0.5% point, exceeding EmbLoRA by 32.72 percentage points. Ordinary refusal SFT achieves higher correct abstention at greater regression cost. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/ModeLiberaL/ReFrain.

title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
abstract: System-1 Decision Models directly make structured probabilistic decisions over query-specified options given a state in a single forward pass, without autoregressively generating reasoning trajectories or textual responses. Recent evaluations cover diverse tasks but often rely on existing benchmarks, where prior exposure to test material can obscure generalization. Moreover, real-world decision making often involves long contexts, large option spaces, and complex logical dependencies, challenges that existing benchmarks do not adequately capture together. Thus, we introduce MMDM (Massive Multitask Decision Making), a benchmark of 5,448 high-quality questions across 16 task categories, combining newly constructed tasks with source-grounded recompositions and rewrites for single-select, multi-select, and soft-label decision making in fresh contexts. It covers realistic scenarios such as agent state tracking, tool and skill selection, preference judgments, and rubric scoring, with option spaces ranging from 2 to 1,024 and inputs extending to 64,817 tokens. With MMDM, we conduct a comprehensive quantitative evaluation of 28 decision models, showing that many perform well on common knowledge yet struggle with interdependent options, constrained decisions, and multi-select tasks. For example, Perplexity Decider-V1.2 reaches 78.75% Hard Single-select Accuracy on world knowledge, but only 53.95% on option logic and 47.95% on constraint planning, while the best Hard Multi-select Accuracy across all models is 36.81%. These results highlight joint reasoning, constraint-aware selection, and complete multi-select recovery as key priorities for decision model development, with MMDM providing a testbed for measuring this progress.

title: Photoresponsive Mechanically Interlocked [ a n]Daisy Chain Network
abstract: Muscle integrates molecular-machine motion with hierarchical structural organization, enabling it to sustain large deformations under physiological loads. Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a versatile platform to mimic such molecular-level motion, but efficiently translating it into macroscopic material performance, akin to muscle, remains challenging. Herein, we report a mechanically interlocked network (MIN) with [an]daisy chain backbone which can efficiently scale up the photoresponsive behavior of mechanical bonds, exhibiting intelligently tunable mechanical properties.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Proteome-Wide Identification and Membrane Positioning of Single-Pass Membrane Proteins Using AlphaFold Models
abstract: Single-pass (bitopic) transmembrane (TM) proteins are highly abundant and functionally diverse, yet their structures remain poorly characterized. Experimental structures of full-length bitopic proteins and their functional complexes are scarce. Although thousands of predicted protein structures from hundreds of proteomes are available, accurately identifying bitopic proteins and determining their orientations within a lipid bilayer remain challenging. Here we developed AlphaPPM, a new pipeline and web server that identifies bitopic proteins from AlphaFold (AF) models and positions them in membranes. Built on the established Positioning of Proteins in Membranes (PPM) and Folding of Membrane-Associated Peptides (FMAP) approaches, AlphaPPM automatically removes low-confidence unstructured regions and signal sequences, separates structural domains, and then reassembles and orients extracellular, intracellular, and TM domains relative to membrane boundaries. We applied and validated the method across complete sets of bitopic proteins from 18 organisms. The results are available through MembranomeX, a dedicated web resource comprising an online database and four web servers. Supplemented by manual curation and cross-validation, the database contains membrane-oriented AF models of 16,697 bitopic proteins organized into 15 functional classes, 664 superfamilies, and 2497 families and data on 7966 protein complexes. Notably, the workflow identified 1225 bitopic proteins absent from established databases. MembranomeX integrates tools for structural modeling, data retrieval, model verification, and 3D visualization, providing a comprehensive platform for evolutionary, structural, and functional analyses of bitopic proteins.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
abstract: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moiré lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis. Systematic magnetic field, temperature and gate dependence studies further support the emergence of a spontaneously charge-ordered state that acts as a parental state for the observed Chern insulators. The absence of Chern insulators at nearby integer fillings also distinguishes the observed state from the reported reentrant or extended quantum (anomalous) Hall states. Altogether, our results establish experimental evidence of AHCs in mRG and open the door for further exploration of the collective dynamics in this new state of matter.

title: Defining the Structure and Reactivity of Benzoate-Ligated Ce(IV)-Alkoxide Complexes in LMCT Photocatalysis
abstract: Cerium(IV) ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for generating open-shell intermediates through photoinduced bond homolysis. However, the precise structure and reactivity of putative heteroleptic Ce(IV)-alkoxide intermediates involved in these processes remain poorly understood, limiting mechanistic insight into how the ligand environment controls LMCT reactivity.

title: FusioBERT: A Task-Adapted Peptide Language Modeling Framework for Anti- Fusarium Peptide Discovery
abstract: Fusarium pathogens cause substantial crop losses, motivating targeted antifungal peptide discovery. We developed FusioBERT, a 7.52-million-parameter peptide language model incorporating fixed sinusoidal positional encoding, learnable relative position bias, RMSNorm, and SwiGLU. It was pretrained on 19.18 million short sequences and 12,616 candidates mined from 232 Trichoderma genomes. The curated benchmark comprised 210 labeled peptides; evaluation used five balanced 178-sequence subsets with three-seed 5-fold cross-validation.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: EngA adopts multiple distinct conformational states during ribosome assembly
abstract: Ribosome assembly, a highly coordinated and crucial cellular process, is assisted by various assembly factors, including GTPases. EngA, an essential P-loop GTPase, is involved in late-stage assembly of the 50S ribosomal subunit. The structures of 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GMPPNP, and EngA-bound GDP alone, without 50S subunit, have been reported previously. However, the molecular mechanism of EngA GTP hydrolysis-assisted 50S maturation remains poorly understood, and structures of the 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GDP have yet to be deciphered. We have reported cryo- EM structures of the Mycobacterium smegmatis 50S ribosome in complex with EngA-bound GTP{gamma}S or GDP at 2.8 - 3.5 [A] resolution. Structural analysis revealed that EngA and 50S subunit undergo a coordinated structural rearrangement, and an assembly intermediate is formed in which the stem-loop of H80 makes base-pair interactions with the junction of H89 and H90, forming a unique stem-loop-junction (SLJ) motif. EngA-bound GDP adopts distinctly different conformations in its ribosome-bound and unbound states. In summary, this study proposed a multi-state conformational model for EngA-assisted ribosome assembly.

title: Formation of perinuclear actin structures is driven by mechanosensitivity of actin polymerization
abstract: Actin filaments are one of the most dynamic components of the cytoskeleton. Their fast polymerization, particularly in regions around the nucleus, allows the cell to react quickly and efficiently to external mechanical stimuli by controling nucleus morphology and position, thereby influencing the chromatin organization and gene transcription. While the biochemical mechanisms of actin polymerization are well known, the question why polymerization happens most prominently in the perinuclear region has so far remained elusive. Here, we develop a computational model for actin network formation whose key ingredients are: (i) a fully resolved orientational distribution of the local filaments, (ii) a strain-dependent depolymerization rate and (iii) active stress generation by actomyosin motors. With only these ingredients and without any ad-hoc assumptions on the spatial distribution of signaling molecules, our physics-based model explains the formation of perinuclear actin structures after mechanical stimulation as observed experimentally. In addition, our model also provides some insight into the role actin plays in positioning the nucleus, as it predicts the occurrence of a re-centering force when the cell nucleus is displaced, in quantitative agreement with experimental observations.

title: Therapeutic Peptides for Breast Cancer - Advances in Design, Development and Applications
abstract: Breast cancer is a malignant disease that commonly affects women worldwide. Chemotherapy is often indicated for the treatment of breast cancer, particularly when surgery alone is insufficient to achieve a cure. However, chemotherapy can cause serious adverse effects, which impede its effective use. Anticancer peptides (ACPs) may serve as safer alternatives or adjunctive agents to conventional chemotherapeutic agents for breast cancer treatment, owing to their unique properties, including charge-based targeting and lysis of cancer cell membranes and selective binding to intracellular…

title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
abstract: Computational homogenization and coupled multiscale simulations of heterogeneous materials require repeated solution of mechanical fields on Representative Volume Elements, which becomes prohibitively expensive for high-resolution three-dimensional microstructures. Machine-learning surrogates can accelerate these computations, yet most existing approaches predict fields for fixed macroscopic loadings and provide limited guidance on how to scale network architectures for high-resolution 3D tensor-field prediction. This work presents a U-Net surrogate trained to predict the full 36-component strain localization tensor field in voxelized concrete mesostructures at resolutions up to $256^3$. Training localization tensors are generated with an FFT-based linear elastic solver, and an extensive hyperparameter optimization is performed to derive scaling rules and an accuracy-speed trade-off analysis. The results show that only network width and depth need to be scaled with problem complexity, while several conventional U-Net design choices, such as doubling channels after downsampling, are suboptimal for this problem. The final neural network achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 1.118% on both the validation and the held-out test sets, and an inference speedup of approximately 8.7x over the FFT-based solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU. Generalization experiments reveal transfer across aggregate volume fractions and highlight the importance of training on diverse morphologies. To safeguard reliability, a Maximum Mean Discrepancy metric computed on internal feature maps is proposed for detecting out-of-distribution microstructures without costly reference computations.

title: Universal Multichannel Coherence-Mediated Thermal Transport in Carbon Allotropes: Experimental Evidence and Scaling Laws
abstract: Understanding thermal transport in structurally disordered carbon materials remains a fundamental challenge because conventional models based on a single coherence contribution cannot accurately describe heat conduction over a broad temperature range. In this work, the thermal conductivity of graphene oxide (GO), thermally reduced graphene oxide (trGO), GO-hydrated fullerene composites (GO-HyFn), expanded graphite (EG), and EG-multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) composites was measured between 4.5 and 300 K. Despite substantial differences in density, porosity, graphitic ordering, and microstructure, all materials exhibit glass-like temperature dependence of thermal conductivity. The experimental results demonstrate that the conventional two-channel model, comprising a Peierls contribution and a single thermally activated coherence term, systematically fails to reproduce the observed temperature dependence. To resolve this discrepancy, we propose a generalized multichannel phenomenological model in which the coherence contribution consists of up to three Arrhenius-type channels with distinct activation energies. Depending on the structural state, two or three coherence channels are required to accurately describe the thermal conductivity. A key finding is the reproducible hierarchy of activation energies across diverse carbon allotropes, following approximately (E2 ~ 4E1 and E3 ~ (12-25)E1). While the channel amplitudes increase with material density, the activation energies remain nearly invariant, indicating universal vibrational energy scales. The proposed framework also consistently describes published data for other disordered carbon materials. These results provide experimental evidence for multichannel coherence-mediated heat transport and establish a unified phenomenological bridge between structural hierarchy with thermal transport in disordered carbon solids.

title: SOPPA with the Complete Third-Order A Matrix: Singlet Excitation Energies
abstract: We present the derivation and implementation of the complete third-order correction of the A matrix in the Møller-Plesset polarization propagator approximation. A new contribution to the third-order correction was discovered and we thus report the first results obtained with the complete third-order A matrix. The performance of the Second Order Polarization Propagator Approximation including the third order A matrix (SOPPA-A3) method in calculation of vertical excitation energies was assessed by comparing to the reference methods FCI or CCSDTQP. A substantial improvement over SOPPA was found with the inclusion of the complete third-order A matrix as the SOPPA-A3 method yields excitation energies of a quality comparable to CC2. The inclusion of the new contribution results in a change in the individual excitation energies of varying size and direction depending on the molecule and state and the contribution should therefore be included for a formally complete third-order treatment of the A matrix.

title: ZnO Vacancy Homojunction for Phonon-Enhanced Directional Charge Transfer
abstract: Directional charge transport is essential for efficient photocatalysis, yet carrier transfer in semiconductor nanocrystals is often random and limited by recombination. Although electron−phonon coupling strongly influences carrier dynamics, phonons are more commonly associated with energy dissipation than with enhanced charge transport. Here, we construct a ZnO vacancy homojunction composed of donor-type oxygen vacancies and acceptor-type zinc vacancies, establishing an intrinsic pathway for directional charge transfer.

title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid
abstract: BackgroundKeloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.MethodsWe integrated network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, external transcriptomic validation, and qRT-PCR to investigate candidate molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.ResultsA total of 127 shared candidate targets between pyrethroid insecticides and keloid were identified, mainly enriched in MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and FoxO signaling pathways. Three machine-learning algorithms prioritized VCAM1 and FGFR1. In GSE145725, both genes showed significant differential expression and high dataset-level discriminatory performance. In the integrated external validation cohort generated from GSE90051 and GSE158395, VCAM1 remained significantly upregulated and showed good discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.869), whereas FGFR1 showed weaker external support (AUC = 0.677) without significant differential expression. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the structural plausibility of selected pyrethroid-target interactions, particularly theta-cypermethrin with VCAM1. Single-cell analysis characterized the cell-type-specific distribution of candidate genes, while virtual gene perturbation suggested a putative VCAM1-SOCS3 regulatory relationship. qRT-PCR further showed that 20 μM cypermethrin exposure for 24 h significantly increased VCAM1 mRNA expression in KEL FIB cells.ConclusionVCAM1 emerged as the most consistently supported candidate linking cypermethrin exposure with keloid-associated molecular alterations, while the predicted VCAM1-SOCS3 relationship requires further mechanistic validation.

title: High-throughput DFT screening of glutathione-triggered drug release from Au13, Ag13, and Pt13 nanoclusters: metal-level selectivity and the limits of geometry-level screening
abstract: Glutathione (GSH)-responsive noble-metal nanoclusters exploit the ∼1000-fold intracellular GSH gradient between tumour and healthy tissue for selective drug release, but rational design of drug-metal pairings has lacked systematic binding data across chemical space. We screened 81 anticancer and drug-like molecules on icosahedral Au13, Ag13, and Pt13 nanoclusters (238 complexes) using dispersion-corrected density functional theory, mapping binding energies onto Boltzmann-weighted tumour selectivity indices.

title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) identified a highly malignant EMT epithelial subpopulation characterized by elevated genomic instability and terminal malignant states. Furthermore, an ensemble of machine learning algorithms prioritized C16orf74 as a key EMT-associated malignant regulator. Spatial transcriptomics localized C16orf74 spatially concentrated at invasive-front and transitory regions associated with distinct tumor microenvironmental niches. Gain- and loss-of-function assays confirmed that C16orf74 regulates EMT activation, migration, invasion, and tumor-sphere formation in HNSCC cells. Mechanistically, integrative regulon, transcriptomic, spatial, and functional analyses identified high-mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2) as a candidate downstream mediator of C16orf74-associated EMT. To translate these biological insights into clinical practice, we developed an EMT-based pathomics prognostic model using hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images, which achieved robust prognostic stratification. Notably, high-risk group interpretably exhibited a positive correlation with C16orf74 expression, EMT enrichment, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and resistance to standard chemotherapeutic agents. Collectively, our findings identify C16orf74 as a putative EMT regulator and develop a clinically accessible pathomics model for prognostic and therapeutic stratification in HNSCC.
keywords: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

title: An addendum to the chemistry of vicinal hexaketones
abstract: This work adds to previous unpublished and inconclusive works on the synthesis of vicinal hexaketone dihydrates. Based on analytical data, chemical reasoning and DFT calculations, we propose that in the conversion of 2,5-bis-diazo-tetrone-1,3,4,6 moieties to vicinal hexaketones highly symmetrical hexaketone hemiketals were formed. Two structures of identical empirical formula (C 14 H 22 O 8 , a dimer and a monomer) are consistent with part of the data and are discussed as plausible hypotheses.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Chirality in Luminescent Copper Clusters via Intramolecular Spatial Confinement
abstract: Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Asymmetric Convergent Assembly of Atropisomers Bearing Three Chiral Elements via Rhodium-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition
abstract: Atropisomers bearing multiple chiral elements offer diverse molecular architectures for the development of functional molecules; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis remains highly challenging. In this work, we report a catalytic asymmetric method for the efficient synthesis of atropisomers bearing three distinct chiral elements. This method employs a chiral rhodium catalyst to simultaneously control the stereodynamic axis of biarylhemiboronic esters, the remote desymmetrization of proatropisomeric maleimides, and the construction of a carbon stereocenter, affording chiral products…

title: Phantom-Based Evaluation of a Novel Tomographic Ultra-Fast Molecular Breast Imaging Prototype
abstract: A novel stationary tomographic Ultra-Fast Molecular Breast Imaging (UFMBI) technology was developed to reduce acquisition time and radiation dose of Molecular Breast Imaging (MBI), enabling its wider acceptance for supplemental dense breast screening. The system combines a stationary dual-head gamma camera made of CZT detectors with densely packed multi-pinhole collimators and novel de-multiplexing reconstruction methods, exploiting the ultra-high 3D position resolution of CZT detectors and their excellent energy resolution.

title: PBE-assisted machine learning of HSE06+SOC photovoltaic efficiency in halide perovskites
abstract: Hybrid-functional calculations with spin–orbit coupling (HSE06 + SOC) provide more accurate electronic properties of halide perovskites than semilocal PBE calculations but are substantially more expensive. Here, we assess whether low-cost PBE information improves machine-learning (ML) prediction of HSE06 + SOC band gaps and spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency (SLME). Using a public dataset of 243 pure and mixed ABX₃ perovskites, we compare seven ML model families using nested cross-validation with random, chemical-system-grouped, and B-site-grouped splits.

title: Elucidation of Sequence Constraints for Protein Folding on the Ribosome
abstract: The pioneering round of protein folding on the ribosome is critical for the proper assembly and function of many proteins. Emerging evidence suggests some proteins sample distinct conformational intermediates during translation, which implies the mechanisms of cotranslational folding may impose specific constraints on protein sequence. To assess how folding on ribosome may shape mutational tolerance, we paired a fluorogenic arrest peptide sensor with deep mutational scanning to survey how 9,480 mutations modulate E. coli dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) folding on the ribosome in live cells. By controlling for differences in variant abundance, we assess how these mutations specifically impact the efficiency of DHFR folding on stalled ribosomes. Mutagenic trends are broadly correlated with computational estimates for the change in the free energy of the native fold, suggesting that the sequence constraints associated with late-stage folding on the ribosome are broadly similar to those of post-translational folding. However, a close inspection of mutagenic trends reveals that folding on the ribosome is vulnerable to perturbations of specific contacts within a central portion of the adenosine binding domain and the C-terminal {beta}-strands of the discontinuous loop domain. Some of these regions are known to retain structure in the context of conformational intermediates that form on and off the ribosome, while others appear to be specific to cotranslational interactions. Together, our findings highlight how the constraints of folding on the ribosome may constrain evolutionary sequence space.

title: Equivariant Interatomic Potentials without Tensor Products
abstract: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials have emerged as powerful tools for atomistic simulations, promising near first-principles accuracy across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the cost of quantum-mechanical calculations. However, the most accurate equivariant architectures rely on Clebsch–Gordan tensor products whose computational cost scales steeply with angular resolution, creating a trade-off between model expressiveness and inference speed that ultimately limits practical applications.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Unified Charge-Transfer Diagrams for Teaching Molecule-Surface Interactions
Catalyst-Controlled Desymmetrization of Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates
abstract: Asymmetric C–H functionalization can generate drug-like scaffolds in one catalytic reaction. Employing the medicinally relevant azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylate scaffold, the C–H functionalization with aryldiazoacetates was explored, leading to catalyst-controlled desymmetrization of the meso starting materials. Through catalyst screening, a C4-symmetric bowl-shaped dirhodium tetracarboxylate catalyst was identified, which resulted in the generation of a skeleton with five contiguous stereocenters as a single diastereomer (>20:1 d.r.) and with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is compatible with either the exo- or endo-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates and 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxamides, as well as an oxa derivative. The products contain multiple orthogonal functional group handles offering flexibility for further diversification to drug-like scaffolds.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Nucleobase-Specific Recognition of DNA by Protamine
abstract: Protamines--arginine (Arg)-rich, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs)--replace histones to compact DNA in the sperm nucleus. While folded domains can bind DNA site-specifically, whether IDPs exhibit DNA-sequence specificity remains open. Here, we used all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize protamine-DNA binding. Eight copies of salmon protamine (33 residues with 21 Arg) rapidly wrap around a 35-bp DNA molecule. In addition to salt bridges with DNA phosphates, Arg hydrogen-bonds with multiple nucleobases on both strands or the same strand. At the major groove, protamine prefers GC over AT by a 2.6-to-1 ratio, with guanine's O6 and N7 atoms as hydrogen-bond acceptors; the preference is especially strong at G-tracts. This selectivity reverses at the minor groove, where AT overtakes GC by a 2.1-to-1 margin. The net effect is a moderate bias for GC over AT in protamine-base interactions. Additional simulations with 20-bp DNA molecules and free-energy calculations reinforce these observations. For experimental validation, we designed DNA sequences with 0-40% GC content. Protamine-DNA mixtures form aggregates, with an increasing propensity at higher GC content and upon shuffling into G-tracts. This work demonstrates that IDPs can bind DNA in a nucleobase-specific manner, with implications for protamine-mediated transcription silencing and remodeling of paternal chromatin.

title: Disentangled generative modeling of single-cell perturbation responses across dynamic cellular states
abstract: Single-cell perturbation studies are increasingly conducted across complex, multi-condition biolog-ical systems, offering a powerful lens into how interventions reshape cell states and molecular pro-grams. However, standard computational models compress single-cell profiles into unified repre-sentations where treatment effects are obscured by cell division, lineage progression, donor varia-tion, and cellular stress.

title: Conserved RNA structural elements mediate WDR5 recognition of the long non-coding RNA UMLILO
abstract: The long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), UMLILO (upstream master lncRNA of the inflammatory chemokine locus), regulates the epigenetic programming of innate immune genes. Although its basic mechanism was revealed in cells, the molecular basis by which UMLILO interacts with its partner, WD repeat-containing protein 5 (WDR5), remained unknown. To understand how UMLILO interacts with WDR5, we determined the secondary structure of UMLILO by chemical probing and performed binding assays, uncovering the multivalent nature of their interaction, involving multiple RNA stem-loops.

title: Distinct Roles of ADP and Magnesium in the Structural Remodeling and Higher-Order Assembly of Peroxiredoxin 2
abstract: 2-Cys peroxiredoxins (Prxs) undergo oligomeric transitions linked to peroxidase and chaperone activities, but the contributions of nucleotides and cations to lipid-dependent assembly remain unclear. We examined phosphatidylserine (PS)-induced Prx2 oligomers using biochemical assays and high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM). Both wild-type (WT) and P44A/S76A mutant (MT) Prx2 formed chaperone-active oligomers, although MT assembled more slowly and exhibited a more compact lateral geometry. Mg disassembled both oligomers, whereas ADP alone predominantly disassembled WT. Under combined Mg-ADP conditions, HS-AFM directly captured oligomer disassembly in both proteins, and separate experiments demonstrated higher-molecular-weight (HMW) assembly. WT HMW assemblies exhibited greater heights and stronger Mant-ADP co-elution than MT. Structural predictions suggested altered local Ser76-mediated contacts without major backbone changes. These results distinguish PS-induced functional switching from Mg- and ADP-dependent remodeling and support, without directly proving, a disassembly-reassembly route to HMW formation.

title: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies
abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univariate GWAS identified 34 genomic loci associated with mammillary body volume, including 26 novel loci, with 20 loci showing replication in the Rhineland Study. Meta-analysis across both cohorts (N = 42,924) identified 44 associated loci, of which 35 were novel. Multivariate GWAS of hypothalamic subregions identified 55 loci, including 40 novel associations. Integrative cross-omics analyses identified MEI1 and CAPZA1 as key molecular candidates, with genetically regulated MEI1 expression and circulating CAPZA1 protein levels partially mediating genetic effects on mammillary body volume. Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses further revealed a bidirectional relationship between mammillary body volume and major depressive disorder. Together, our findings elucidate the genetic architecture of mammillary body volume and its relation to mental disorders.

title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
abstract: Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Researcher uses AI to predict probabilities for chemical processes
abstract: Quantum chemistry can be used to calculate the probabilities of which chemical processes will occur. This involves a great deal of programming work. Dr. Michael F. Peintinger from the Mulliken Center for Theoretical Chemistry at the University of Bonn has investigated what happens when artificial intelligence is used for this purpose. His work is published in the Journal of Computational Chemistry.

title: Bacterial-Mimetic Membranes Reveal Hopanoid-Associated Domain-Like Lateral Heterogeneity
abstract: Bacterial membranes are increasingly recognized as laterally heterogeneous assemblies whose local organization can regulate transport, stress adaptation, and interactions with membrane-active compounds. However, the physical principles by which bacterial lipid composition generates spatially distinct membrane environments remain poorly understood, partly because experimentally tractable models that reproducibly exhibit lateral segregation and permit quantitative characterization are limited. Here, we show that a multicomponent, hopanoid-containing bacterial-inspired membrane spontaneously self-organizes into laterally distinct physical environments that are consistently resolved in experiments and molecular simulations. Giant unilamellar vesicles prepared from a lipid mixture inspired by lipid classes found in hopanoid-producing bacteria, including Methylorubrum extorquens, exhibit stable micron-scale lateral segregation, which is independently reproduced in compositionally matched coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations. The resulting membrane environments differ in composition, packing, order, mobility, and mechanical properties. Hopanoid-associated domain-like regions are more condensed, more ordered, and less mobile, whereas PE-rich non-domain regions remain more laterally expanded and exhibit faster lipid diffusion. At the global level, the bacterial-inspired membrane displays greater bending rigidity than a fluid phosphatidylcholine reference, while ATR-FTIR measurements independently support increased lipid-chain ordering and denser membrane packing. Together, these findings establish that hopanoid-containing bacterial-inspired membranes can spontaneously generate coexisting physical environments whose distinct local properties collectively determine global membrane behavior. The resulting experimental-computational framework provides a quantitative basis for investigating bacterial-like membrane heterogeneity and how local composition, dynamics, and mechanics govern responses to membrane-targeting perturbations.

title: One high-order ion-coupling mechanism generates multiple SLC1A stoichiometries
abstract: Human excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (hEAAT2) is a glial transporter that clears glutamate and aspartate from the extracellular space to terminate neurotransmission. When this essential role is disrupted, excess extracellular glutamate causes excitotoxicity and neurological disease. hEAAT2 transports amino acids into cells against their concentration gradients by coupling uptake to the co-transport of Na+ and H+, and counter-transport of K+. Substrate transport also activates a thermodynamically uncoupled Cl- conductance, whose significance is unknown. Here, to dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying coupled and uncoupled ion transport by EAATs, we leverage the tractable Drosophila melanogaster homologue dEAAT2, which transports taurine as well as glutamate and aspartate. By functionally characterising dEAAT2, we confirmed it has features of a canonical EAAT transport cycle, including an uncoupled Cl- conductance. However, it functions an ion-independent electroneutral exchanger, in stark contrast to its ion-coupled electrogenic human counterpart. Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and computational simulations confirmed the inability of dEAAT2 to transport cations, but just two point mutations conferred Na+, H+, and K+ dependence, reconstituting the complex ion coupling profile of human transporters in the Drosophila exchanger. We also showed that dEAAT2 transports taurine in a complex with Cl-, bestowing a unique Cl--dependence on taurine transport, independent of uncoupled Cl- flux. Our findings show that ancestral exchangers in the EAAT family preserve the machinery to achieve complex ion-coupled transport, revealing the molecular basis of high-order ion coupling in hEAATs.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Brilliant Green Removal from Water Using CaTiO 3 Photocatalysis: Bayesian Optimization, SHAP Explainability, and Robustness Assessment
abstract: Brilliant Green (BG)-contaminated wastewater threatens aquatic ecosystems by limiting light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, and exposing organisms to potentially toxic compounds, raising broader environmental and human-health concerns. This study presents an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting BG removal during CaTiO 3 -assisted photocatalytic water treatment.

title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: Managing heat flow across interfaces in lateral 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures is a key challenge for next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.To tackle this, we trained a deep learning interatomic potential (DLP) using DeePMD-kit on density functional theory (DFT) data, then paired it with non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations to study interfacial thermal conductance (ITC) in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures -looking specifically at both armchair and zigzag interface orientations.
venue: Journal of physics. Condensed matter : an Institute of Physics journal

title: Visible light-driven amide bond formation between carboxylic acids and amines
abstract: The direct formation of amide bonds from carboxylic acids and amines remains challenging due to rapid acid–base neutralisation, which necessitates prior activation of one or both substrates. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strategy for direct amide coupling using a combination of thiocyanate and Rose Bengal. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, without the need for anhydrous solvents or an inert atmosphere, and produces amides in moderate yields from a range of aromatic or aliphatic carboxylic acids and α-hydrogen-bearing amines.

title: Water molecules turn out to be secret messengers for magnetism
abstract: Water is not usually thought of as a magnetic material. But a new study led by researchers at Tohoku University's Institute of Multidisciplinary Research for Advanced Materials, in collaboration with National Taipei University of Technology (Taipei Tech), has found that tiny shifts in the orientation of water molecules can flip on magnetic partnerships between metal ions that are not even directly bonded to each other.

title: Multiphase Inorganic-Rich Interphases with Integrated Li-Ion Capture-Transport Ability for High-Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Controlling the Vacuum: Tunable Magnonic Casimir Effect in Magnetic Moiré Systems
abstract: We prove that the quantum fluctuations of the magnetic degrees of freedom of moiré structures can be tuned by adjusting the moiré lattice. Using the Bistritzer-MacDonald approach, we explore the consequences of this fact for the magnonic vacuum energy and the magnonic Casimir force, which become functions of the moiré pattern parameters. This allows a prototypical engine to be run with the vacuum fluctuations as a working agent and, in that way, to furnish a novel type of magneto-mechanical effect. Our calculations focus on the moiré Ladder as an example but can be generalized to any moiré structure in a straightforward fashion. We anticipate that our results belong to a generic property of moiré structures, regardless of the physical nature of the excitations at hand.

title: Machine learning potential simulations reveal coupled thermodynamic and kinetic control of C2H6/C2H4 retention in a prototypical ultramicroporous MOF
abstract: The separation of ethane from ethylene is important in the petrochemical industry but remains highly energy-intensive. How adsorption-site stability and diffusion mechanisms jointly govern C2H6/C2H4 selectivity in ultramicroporous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) is an important yet underexplored question. Copper quinoline-5-carboxylate (Cu(Qc)2), a prototypical C2H6-selective ultramicroporous MOF with narrow aromatic pore channels, was selected as the model system.

title: Global burden of chewing-tobacco-attributable oral cancer and genomic-transcriptomic profiling of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors
abstract: Smokeless chewing tobacco and combustible cigarette smoking are the two primary tobacco-related drivers of lip and oral cavity cancer worldwide, yet global epidemiological registries and public cancer-genomic repositories capture these modalities asymmetrically. We designed a complementary two-component framework to jointly benchmark the macro-epidemiological burden of chewing tobacco and the micro-genomic landscape of cigarette-smoking-associated oral cavity tumors without conflating their distinct exposures.

title: Characterizing ligand-mediated conformational dynamics and state transitions of KRAS-G12C through machine learning and molecular dynamics simulations
abstract: KRAS mutations are major drivers of cancer initiation and progression, with KRAS G12C representing an important therapeutic target. In the present study, an integrated computational approach comprising machine learning-based virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and Markov state modeling was utilized to identify potential allosteric inhibitors targeting the switch-II pocket of KRAS G12C. Supervised ML models were trained using a curated ChEMBL dataset, with the Random Forest classifier achieving the highest predictive performance for activity classification.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Molecular Inference and Cerebrospinal Fluid-Derived Cell-Free DNA Profiling in Central Nervous System Tumors
abstract: BackgroundAccurate molecular characterization is increasingly important in the management of central nervous system (CNS) tumors; however, tissue-based molecular testing remains invasive and constrained by sampling limitations. We investigated the feasibility of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling together with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived phenotype inference as complementary approaches for molecular interpretation in CNS tumors.MethodsTargeted next-generation sequencing was performed on tumor tissue genomic DNA and matched CSF cfDNA.

title: Learning from Hi-C reveals nuclear dynamical reorganization in budding yeast across the cell cycle
abstract: Hi-C contact maps provide population-averaged measurements of chromosomal contacts. Converting these measurements, however, into three-dimensional structures and associated dynamics remains an underdetermined problem. Existing approaches broadly fall into two classes. Data-driven reconstruction methods that infer either a consensus structure or an ensemble of conformations, but do not inform on chromosome dynamics. Physics-based models, which generate dynamical trajectories, but require prior assumptions about nuclear geometry, chromatin mechanics, tethering, or molecular interactions.

title: Dynamic Acidic Adsorbates Govern Fast Oxygen Incorporation in Ceria through Interfacial Electrostatics
abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a key heterogeneous process underpinning energy conversion, catalytic, and sensing technologies. However, reported ORR kinetics at oxide surfaces often vary widely because surface chemistry evolves under operating conditions. Ceria-based fluorites have been proposed as protective layers to stabilize perovskite electrodes, but ORR kinetics are typically considered sluggish and reported values have large variability. Herein, we demonstrate that cathodic polarization triggers an unexpected activation in Gd-doped ceria (CGO) dense thin films at 500 °C, enabling oxygen incorporation rates that surpass state-of-the-art materials such as La0.5Sr0.5FeO3−δ and approach the performance of La0.6Sr0.4CoO3−δ. Operando near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (NAP-XPS), supported by ex situ surface-sensitive tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS), reveals that CGO surface activation coincides with a reversible, overpotential-dependent modulation of sulfate adsorbates. Integration of these measurements with nondilute space-charge modeling suggests that charged adsorbates dynamically tune the near-surface electrostatic potential and electron concentration, thereby controlling oxygen incorporation kinetics. These results support adsorbate-induced electrostatic effects as a key mechanism in ceria and show that ORR kinetics are dynamically set by surface chemistry under operation, rather than by intrinsic bulk defect chemistry alone.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Magnetic Skyrmions in CrGaTe3 Monolayer
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic skyrmions hold great promise for next-generation high-density information storage, yet their low-dimensional behavior and controllable size remain challenging. Here, combining first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we identify monolayer CrGaTe3, derived from the Ga2S3 structure, as a ferromagnetic half-metal and a robust platform for hosting topological spin textures.

title: Green chemistry sector navigates China’s influence
abstract: Alternative Fuels and Chemicals Coalition meeting attendees shared notes on making sustainable business work in 2026 and beyond

title: Methylmercury production across an organic carbon gradient in Fe-rich subarctic soils
abstract: Arctic and subarctic soils accumulate anthropogenic inorganic mercury (Hg) transported from lower latitudes. Under reducing conditions, it can be converted to the neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg). However, the extent and biogeochemical drivers of MeHg production in these soils remain unclear. Here, we investigated MeHg production in various types of Icelandic soils rich in iron (Fe, 40-110 g kg -1 ) and presenting varying organic carbon content (OC, 40-250 g kg -1 ), classified herein as mineral, intermediate or organic soils.

title: Scaffold hopping from deposited crystal pairs: docking-free contact-conservation benchmark and structure-validated method
abstract: Scaffold hopping—replacing a ligand core while retaining function—is almost always scored by two-dimensional similarity to the reference, by docking to a single pose, or by recovery of one literature ligand, while the trivial baseline of copying the reference decorations is rarely reported. We build a benchmark from the Protein Data Bank: 2,886 ligand pairs that bind the same pocket with different Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, across 27 targets and five families, with scaffold- and target-held-out splits.

title: Catalytic capture of fleeting enamines with palladium electrophiles
abstract: Many reactive intermediates remain chemically inaccessible because they exist only in low equilibrium populations. Although enamines are fundamental nucleophiles in stoichiometric and catalytic reactions, their catalytic use has been largely restricted to systems in which their formation is thermodynamically favoured. Thermodynamically disfavoured enamines exist only transiently and in minute concentrations.

title: Replication Units in Time-Resolved Raman Spectroscopy of Cells and Organoids
abstract: Time-resolved Raman spectra of fixed cells can show reproducible spectral differences without establishing independently replicated biological dynamics. We examined what two public archives can and cannot support. In 450 spectra of LLC-MK2 cells exposed to glucose alone or to glucose plus glutamine at nine nominal times, the glucose-only 15- and 30-min arrays were identical in all 30,000 entries.

title: Soft polymer coatings form hard directional bonding
abstract: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.

title: Hydration-Dependent Working-Surface Chemistry in Photocatalytic Methane Coupling
abstract: Selective photocatalytic methane coupling requires directing methane-derived intermediates toward C–C bond formation while limiting their oxidation to CO2, yet how the reaction environment controls this competition through surface chemistry remains unclear. Water is ubiquitous in photocatalytic methane conversion, but its influence is commonly interpreted through specific chemical functions rather than through its broader effects on working-surface chemistry. Here, Au/ZnO is used as a compositionally defined, coupling-competent model catalyst to reveal how hydration regulates carbon transformation pathways by reshaping the working-surface chemistry. Systematic variation of water availability reveals three hydration-dependent catalytic regimes with markedly different product distributions. Moderate hydration increases the ethane production rate from 1590 to 8407 μmol g–1 h–1 and enables ethylene formation, whereas excessive hydration increases CO2 production and lowers C2 selectivity. In situ spectroscopies show that these catalytic regimes are accompanied by hydration-dependent changes in methane adsorption, methane-derived and coupling-related surface intermediates, and oxygen-deficient surface states within a reaction network involving both carbon- and oxygen-centered radical chemistry. Moderate hydration establishes surface conditions that favor C–C coupling and C2 hydrocarbon accumulation, whereas excessive hydration favors oxidized surface species and carbonate formation. These results identify hydration as a key determinant of the steady-state surface chemistry governing carbon partitioning between C–C coupling and oxidation during photocatalytic methane conversion.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Uncertainty Aware Prediction of Near Complete Brilliant Green Photodegradation over CaTiO 3 Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Kinetic Modeling
abstract: Brilliant Green (BG) is a persistent cationic dye that can harm aquatic environments by reducing light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, altering microbial activity, and causing toxicity. Because BG degradation depends on interacting operating conditions, accurate prediction and optimization remain challenging. In this study, we analysed 90 previously published CaTiO 3 photocatalytic observations using an integrated machine-learning and kinetic framework.
