title: Predictive Modeling of Friction-Resistant Advanced Coatings using Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Turbulent skin-friction resistance in industrial conduit transport and piping infrastructure accounts for substantial energy dissipation worldwide. Biomimetic shark-skin riblets offer an attractive passive drag-reduction mechanism by constraining cross-stream turbulent momentum transfer and pinning quasi-streamwise vortices aloft. However, optimizing these micro-topographies across high-dimensional parameter spaces (riblet spacing s, aspect ratio h/s, conduit diameter D, and Reynolds number Re) remains experimentally and numerically prohibitive owing to the computational expense of…

title: Atomically Precise Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 Gold Nanocluster as Type I Photosensitizer: ROS Generation Mechanism
abstract: The exceptional response of the gold nanocluster Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 , capable of generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) via electron transfer, was studied from both computational modeling and experimental characterization. An electron density perspective on remarkable features of gold nanoclusters and their photophysical applications provides a comprehensive study of the mechanism the gold nanocluster Au 22 (Lys-Cys-Lys) 16 undergoes as a type I photosensitizer.

title: Laser-Assisted Nuclear Thermal Propulsion for Cislunar Logistics: A Monte Carlo Power-Closure Assessment
abstract: Laser-assisted nuclear thermal propulsion (LANTP) would raise the specific impulse of a nuclear thermal tug by adding orbital laser power to the hydrogen. We take performance targets of this kind (specific impulse 1300–1500 s, thrust 50–120 kN, a 1–50 MW laser on a 100–500 MWt reactor, and an initial mass in low Earth orbit, IMLEO, 40% below that of conventional nuclear thermal propulsion, NTP) as hypothetical design targets and test them for Earth–Moon logistics with a coupled model: hydrogen thermochemistry checked against Cantera, a power chain from the wall plug to the propellant…

title: A Staged Reaction Optimisation Workflow for Fragment-to-Lead Elaboration
abstract: Here, we present a reaction optimisation workflow that integrates data mining to generate unbiased, data-led starting points, high-throughput experimentation (HTE) to narrow the reaction parameter space, and closed-loop flow experiments guided by multi-objective Bayesian optimisation for fine-tuning. Designed for early-stage medicinal chemistry, particularly fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD), the workflow was demonstrated in two direct two-step syntheses of potent fragment-derived protein kinase C inhibitor precursors, involving sequential C–C and C–X bond formations.

title: Synthesis of a Molecular Four-Ring Brunnian Link
abstract: Mathematics describes infinitely many distinct knots and links, but translating these topologies into molecular structures remains a major challenge in chemistry. Here, we develop a strategy to bridge mathematical topology and molecular synthesis using single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), with a four-ring Brunnian link (4-BL) as a demanding test case. Because cutting any one ring releases all the others, the Brunnian property can be directly verified by selective cleavage.

title: JAI: Physically Constrained Prediction of Conformer-Averaged Proton–Proton Coupling Constants in Solution
abstract: Machine-learning predictors of proton–proton coupling constants are usually trained on, and evaluated against, couplings computed for single geometries rather than the conformer-averaged values measured in solution. We describe JAI (J-coupling prediction with Artificial Intelligence), a graph transformer for 2J–5J(H,H) of small organic molecules trained on scaled Fermi-contact DFT couplings of about 3700 molecules, computed on geometries from the universal machine-learned potential UMA and averaged over conformers in six solvents, and on more than 25 000 curated experimental couplings…

title: Backbone Expansion via Enzyme-Mediated Side-Chain Transfer
abstract: There exists no straightforward strategy to generate protein materials containing internally spliced non-protein matter, especially at lengths and scales that support functional characterization. Here we describe Backbone Expansion via Enzyme-mediated Side-chain Transfer (BEST), a facile and general strategy for generating proteins containing internally spliced, non-protein matter at scale.

title: Copper adsorption and release by biodegradable polyester films under field conditions
abstract: In this work we analyze the adsorption of Cu(II) ions on biodegradable mulching films in real conditions by performing a comparison of two commercial PLA/PBAT-based films with a standard olefinic film (LDPE). In particular, in situ tests have been performed at an experimental agriculture center of the Apulian region by miming a real crop cycle. The desorption phenomenon of copper has been also investigated by measuring the amount of metal ions released by the debris of mulching films in the environment at the end of the crop cycle after burying the mulching films under the soil.

title: Chemical Filtering of Thymine over Uracil in Prebiotic Hydrothermal Systems: A Mass-Consistent Stochastic Model with Complementary Insights from UV Photodamage Pathways
abstract: The origin of thymine in DNA remains a central puzzle in astrobiology. While Darwinian evolution may have refined RNA into DNA, the initial selection mechanism must have been purely chemical. Here we present UPDSF v6.1.1—the Unified Prebiotic DNA Selection Framework—a mass-conserving, kineticallyconsistent stochastic model of hydrothermal-vent chemistry. At the optimum (90 °C, pH 11, dark vent), a chemical selection index (CSI) of 6.019× emerges through the multiplicative combination of real (direct) T-preferential hydrolysis and pool-composition drift.

title: Assessment of machine-learned vs. classical/quantum atomistic simulations for predicting palladium-hydrogen materials
abstract: Palladium-hydrogen materials are used in a wide range of hydrogen storage, purification, sensing, and catalysis technologies; however, accurately predicting the structural and kinetic behavior of palladium hydrides remains computationally challenging. In this work, we present the first systematic assessment of Meta’s Universal Model for Atoms (UMA), a machine-learned interatomic potential, by benchmarking its predictions against density functional theory (DFT) and two widely used embedded-atom method (EAM) potentials for PdHx systems.

title: Connecting Ligand Structure to Reaction Rate and Coordination Behavior in the Undergraduate Laboratory
abstract: A research-oriented laboratory module has been developed for an upper-division undergraduate inorganic chemistry course with the aim to help students connect ligand structure to reaction rate and coordination behavior. The experiments, which have been implemented and refined at the University of Cincinnati since 2021, focus on the synthesis and characterization of twelve nickel(II) salen-type 10 complexes derived from Schiff-base ligands, which differ by backbone linkers and ring substituents.

title: An Interpretable Chemoinformatics Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Learning Frameworks, Decoy Sensitivity, and Green Catalyst Prioritization
abstract: As descriptor-based machine learning becomes widely used for reaction yield prediction and catalyst prescreening, controlled validation testbeds with known ground-truth data-generating processes (DGPs) are useful for auditing model behavior, cross-validation protocols, and post-hoc explainability methods. Here we construct and evaluate a synthetic chemoinformatics benchmark of N = 5,000 catalytic alcohol oxidation reactions across 20 independently seeded dataset realizations (100,000 total simulated reactions).

title: Breaking the Trade-Off – Tilted T-Shaped Bis-Heteroaryl Azo Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Bidirectional Switching
abstract: Azoheteroarenes provide a versatile platform for controlling the molecular geometry and photochemical reactivity of azo switches through heteroaryl substitution. Here, we describe a family of bis-heteroaryl azo photoswitches combining pyrazole with thiophene or selenophene heterocycles, leveraging the independent success of these classes of azo switch. While T-shaped ( Z )-isomers are currently only established with a phenyl acceptor motif, single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of a T-shaped ( Z )-isomer in these new designs where the pyrazole ring acts as the acceptor of a…

title: Desalination LLM: Large Language Model Agents Design Efficient Graphene Membranes for Water Desalination
abstract: Graphene nanopores can, in principle, combine high water permeability with strong salt rejection, but finding pore geometries that do both usually requires many molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We describe a design framework in which a large language model (LLM) grows a nanopore atom by atom, using pretrained predictors of water flux and ion rejection to judge each candidate.

title: GPU-accelerated analytic Hartree–Fock gradients
abstract: Analytic nuclear gradients underpin much of computational quantum chemistry, driving geometry optimization and supplying the forces of ab initio molecular dynamics. Yet on graphics processing units (GPUs) the gradient has received far less attention than the selfconsistent field (SCF) procedure it accompanies. In current production codes its construction can cost as much as the entire preceding SCF. Here we present a novel, high-performance GPU implementation of the analytic Hartree–Fock energy gradient.

title: A Workflow for the Systematic Synthesis and Assessment of Trianguleniums as Optical Probes for G-quadruplex DNA Imaging
abstract: Guanine-quadruplexes (G4s), play critical regulatory roles in genomic processes including transcription, replication, and telomere maintenance. Consequently, there is significant interest in understanding G4 dynamics in live cells. One of the approaches to do this is by using optical probes that have distinct fluorescence lifetime upon binding to different nucleic acid topologies. Such probes can then be used in conjunction with Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) for sensing and imaging G4s in cells.

title: End-to-End Learning from Experimental Data: Integrating the PC-SAFT Equation of State into Neural Networks Training for Improved Polymer Parameter Estimation
abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient thermodynamic models are essential for the design, optimization, and operation of many (bio)chemical processes involving polymer solutions, blends, and membranes. In this work, we combine machine learning (ML) with the PC-SAFT equation of state (EoS) to predict the non-associating pure component parameters for polymers, enabling the rapid evaluation of the pressure–volume–temperature (PVT) behavior of polymer melts and rubbers.

title: Emergence of Atomic Energy States: Predicting Ionization Energies of One-Electron Systems via Nucleus-Driven Force Propagation in Real Space
abstract: Although probabilistic electron wave-function approaches provide solid mechanistic insights for molecules, their inherent reliance on static, boundary-dependent approximations limits the direct description of real-space molecular dynamics. This study demonstrates the emergence of highly accurate atomic energy states by a single nucleus-driven force-propagating framework within an open system.When compared withNIST ionization energy dataforone-electron systems,our model yields a 0.0000% relative error for the hydrogen atom (Z = 1), where the energy spectrum naturally emerges from the nucleus…

title: Alchemical Free Energy Methods Reproduce Scaffold Modifications in a Macrocyclic Peptide PCSK9 Series
abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) methods are widely used in drug discovery campaigns to optimise the binding affinity of small molecule ligands. Recently, macrocyclic peptides have emerged as an increasingly attractive modality alongside small molecules and biologics. They possess the unique ability to bind to large, flat, and featureless binding sites that are inaccessible to small molecules, while offering a route to oral bioavailability, which antibodies lack. However, modelling macrocycles with FEP presents significant challenges.

title: Schiff bases from Sodium alginate and o-phenylenediamine as a water-soluble fluorescent copper(II) chemosensor
abstract: Polymeric Schiff bases derived from aromatic diamines have attracted significant interest due to their potential applications as fluorescent chemosensors. In this study, polymeric Schiff bases were synthesized from oxidized alginates (oxidation degrees of 20%, 40%, and 60%) and o-phenylenediamine. 1 H-NMR and FT-IR confirmed the chemical changes produced in all synthesized polymers. Rheological analysis revealed that the oxidized alginates exhibited Newtonian behavior, with a marked reduction of their thixotropy.

title: TRIDENT: Three-Lever Privileged Self-Distillation for Audio-Visual Source Separation in Flow-Chemistry Pilot Plants
abstract: Its weakness is that one fume-hood bay runs several unit operations at once, so the pump, the switching valve, the gas bubbler and the agitator arrive as a single mixed channel; the loudest of them owns most of the acoustic energy, and the components that carry the earliest fault signatures are exactly the quiet ones. We cast this as audio-visual source separation in which the viewing window supplies the second modality and the supervision is privileged: single-unit calibration recordings and 15-min at-line HPLC samples exist during training and never at deployment.

title: Solid-support photoacids
abstract: Merocyanine photoacids are versatile molecules that allow the control of different processes with visible light, including CO 2 capture, driving molecular machines, and catalyzing reactions. However, high concentrations of the photoacid are needed for large pH changes, which makes observing other changes spectroscopically challenging, as well as requiring the laborious separation of the photoacid afterwards. Herein, we report a solidphase merocyanine-based photoacid that can generate a reversible pH change in bulk solution.

title: BindCraft2 versus RFD4-Proteina for de novo peptide binder design against insecticide targets
abstract: De novo peptide binders are attractive leads for biological pesticides because they can be designed against validated insecticide targets without a small-molecule discovery campaign. Two generative pipelines dominate this space: BindCraft2, an AlphaFold2/ProteinMPNN campaign that accepts designs only after a cascade of structural filters, and RFD4-Proteina, a flow-matching foundation model that generates conditioned backbones and sequences in a single pass.

title: Molecular thermal motion harvester for electricity conversion via contact electrification: Role and effect of design and additives
abstract: Converting the molecular thermal energy to electric energy via liquid-solid interfacial contact electrification was experimentally validated and it presents a promising approach towards a new type of green energy technology. In this work, nylon 66 and polystyrene layers coated on copper foils were employed as positive and negative electrodes, to investigate the effect of electrolytes, saccharides, and surfactants, as additives to water. This study aims to improve device performance and establish some basic design principles for molecular thermal energy conversion systems.

title: Comparative QSAR Study of Aquatic Toxicity Prediction Using Molecular Descriptors and Fingerprints with Machine Learning
abstract: To ensure environmental safety, we need to predict aquatic toxicity, but experimental testing is expensive, time consuming and often raises ethical concerns. In this study, we used machine learning to predict the 96-hour lethal concentration (LC50) of 908 organic compounds to fathead minnow ( Pimephales promelas ). We compared four different ways to represent molecular structure: (A) six pre-calculated descriptors from the original dataset, (B) twelve physicochemical descriptors computed from SMILES using RDKit, (C) 2048-bit Morgan fingerprints, and (D) a combined set of original and RDKit…

title: Controlled Oxidant Delivery Uncovers Selectivity Branching in Heterogeneous Epoxidation Catalysis
abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis generally features complex speciation of reactive intermediates that limits selectivity control and mechanistic understanding. Olefin epoxidation is a major and highly carbon-intensive process in the chemical industry, yet the molecular origin of selectivity branching causing the competing, CO 2 -emitting combustion reaction remains debated and is obscured by the presence of multiple oxidants on catalyst surfaces.

title: Stereoelectronic Modulation of Hyperconjugative Networks in Saturated Heterocycles: Bridging Hilbert-Space NBO Perturbations with Real-Space QTAIM Electron Cloud Distortions
abstract: The stereoelectronic modulation of hyperconjugative networks dictates the fundamental parameters of saturated heterocycles. Herein is presented a quantum chemical investigation into the anomeric effect across a matrix of 2-substituted oxygen and sulfur heterocycles utilising a GPU-accelerated pySCF-GPU optimisation pipeline at the CAM-B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD/PCM level of theory, coupled with orbital perturbation evaluations via Firefly B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVPD; QTAIM topology analyses via Multiwfn.

title: Expanding the Covalent Warhead Toolbox: Discovery of the First Covalent PARG Inhibitors Using Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane-Based Warheads
abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) is the principal enzyme responsible for the degradation of poly(ADP-ribose) chains and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in oncology within the DNA damage response (DDR) field. Although several reversible PARG inhibitors have recently entered clinical development, covalent inhibition of PARG has not previously been described. Herein, we report the discovery and optimization of the first covalent PARG inhibitors.

title: Diversity of N-terminal Sequences of Aβ Peptides Governs TDMQ20-Mediated CuII Extraction Efficiency and Kinetics
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is recognized as the most common form of dementia, with no curative therapies available. One of the current strategies towards an AD drug focuses on the development of copper-binding ligands capable of extracting CuII ions from β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides, among which TDMQ20 has attracted considerable attention. However, previous studies of TDMQ20 have focused primarily on its interaction with Aβ(1–x) peptides, with no consideration given to the molecular heterogeneity of Aβ species present in the AD brain.

title: Scalable Amidation Reaction by Resonant Acoustic Mixing. Application to the multi-gram scale synthesis of marketed Agrochemicals
abstract: Industrial amide bond formation in agrochemical manufacture still relies on low-molecularweight chlorinating agents and dipolar aprotic solvents. Herein, five marketed SDHI fungicides, Fenfuram (1), Boscalid (2), Mepronil (3), Flutolanil (4) and Fluxapyroxad (5), were prepared by TCFH-mediated one-pot/two-step amidation across three mechanochemical platforms (VBM, PBM and LA-RAM).

title: pKasso: Accurate and accessible prediction of small-molecule protonation states
abstract: The protonation states of molecules are tightly linked to their physicochemical properties. Accurately predicting protonation states is therefore important for applications such as docking-based virtual screening in drug discovery. Modern machine-learning models can predict molecular p K a values with good accuracy, but obtaining pH-dependent protonation-state ensembles from available open-source models can cause substantial installation and workflow overhead. Commercial tools provide convenient alternatives but can entail substantial licensing costs.

title: Photoluminescent Ratiometric and Lifetime Thermometry Governed by Water Dynamics in Heterometallic M(s-block)-Ce(III) Tricyanomethanide-Based Coordination Polymers
abstract: It is important to develop novel optical materials combining effective photoluminescence (PL) with a highly sensitive optical response to external stimuli. Cerium(III) complexes, whose efficient luminescence, ascribable to the d-f electronic transitions, is modulated by the coordination environment, are promising in this context. Here, experimental and theoretical studies on achieving the combination of a high room-temperature (RT) visible emission quantum yield (QY) of up to 0.94 (370 nm excitation) with the ratiometric optical thermometry of a relative thermal sensitivity reaching 9.2% K−1…

title: In-silico investigation of small molecule inhibitors of malaria-inducing cycloguanil-resistant Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase
abstract: Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) is the target of antimalarial drugs such as cycloguanil. However, mutations of DHFR, particularly the A16V and S108T variants, induce steric interactions that confer resistance to cycloguanil. It is crucial to find new therapeutics to combat cycloguanil-resistant strains of P. falciparum . We used in-silico methods to investigate possible drug candidates of A16V+S108T DHFR, a key cycloguanil-resistant double mutant.

title: Fine-Tuning a Graph-Transformer ADMET Model Improves Half-Life and Plasma Protein Binding Concordance
abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) models are usually judged on predefined benchmark splits. Those splits are useful, but they do not show whether a model reproduces the pharmacokinetic (PK) numbers that are actually reported for individual drugs. Here we compared ADMET-AI with a fine-tuned NV-KERMT-70M-v2 model (“KERMT”) on the same Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC)-aligned endpoint definitions.

title: A Graphene Oxide–Coco Pith Fiber–Polyvinyl Alcohol Non-Structural Composite Filter for Lead [Pb(II)] Removal from Aqueous Solution: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Lead [Pb(II)] in drinking water is a persistent health risk, and low-cost filter media are of interest where centralised treatment is limited. This preliminary proof-of-concept study prepared a filter body from graphene oxide (GO), coco pith fiber and boric-acid-treated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and tested it once with a nominal 50 mg/L Pb(II) solution under gravity filtration. GO was made by a modified Hummers' method and examined by FTIR only; the composite itself was not characterized. The filtrate was analyzed by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy.

title: Unlocking the promise of materials AI through application proxies and protected collaboration
abstract: AI-guided and robotic laboratories can accelerate experiments within a company, but materials development still depends on repeated testing across company boundaries. Here we show in controlled simulation how investment in application-relevant private testing reduces that external work. We extend Minimum Knowledge Collaboration with application proxies, calling the extension MKC2. Suppliers develop combinations of physical tests and reference assemblies that capture how their materials respond under relevant product conditions.

title: Mixed-Valence Chemistry without Fractional Electrons in Variational 2-Electron Reduced Density Matrix Theory via Local Integer-Charge Constraints
abstract: The tractable capture of strong, or multi-reference correlation effects continues to present a formidable challenge at the forefront of quantum chemistry. Variational two-electron reduced density matrix (v2RDM) theory presents a polynomially scaling approach to multi-reference calculations, but its use of approximate N-representability conditions yields lower bounds to the true energy and possibly unphysical descriptions.

title: When Can a Molecular-Dynamics Simulation Stop?
abstract: Molecular-dynamics (MD) simulations are usually run for a prespecified duration, even when the goal is to estimate an equilibrium observable to a stated precision. Stopping as soon as an estimated uncertainty becomes small enough is attractive, but repeated inspection invalidates uncertainty statements calibrated for a fixed time. We formulate data-dependent stopping as an inferential problem with an explicit precision target and a simultaneous-in-time coverage requirement, and organise it into four gated stages: temporal prediction against strong baselines, uncertainty calibration, an…

title: Coupled Condensation–Melting Heat Transfer and Thermal Design Limits of a Steam-Assisted Pipeline Cleaning Crawler: A Probabilistic Modeling Study
abstract: Steam-assisted pipeline cleaning couples condensation heat transfer, melting of a deposit and a thermally protected tool, and the coupling, not any single component, sets its limits. We study a motorized steam-assisted crawler with a probabilistic model: transient conduction through an aluminum–aerogel–titanium wall into a lumped battery pack, film condensation, a melt model with a retained liquid film whose resistance is the dimensionless group Pif=hs/kl, a dynamic film balancing melt production and gravity drainage, an orifice model of the bypass relief, and a steam budget.

title: Pairing manure and lignocellulosic biochars to reduce phosphorus losses from manure fertilisers
abstract: Manures supply less nitrogen relative to phosphorus than crops require, so applying them to meet N demand accumulates P in soils and increases losses to water. Pyrolysis reduces the solubility of manure P, but the fraction that remains soluble is still vulnerable to runoff. This study tested whether lignocellulosic biochars applied alongside manure biochars can recapture that fraction. Poultry litter and dairy slurry were pyrolysed at 300, 500, and 700 °C, and their release of phosphate, ammonium, and nitrate was measured in 30-day batch incubations and in packed beds.

title: Self-Assembled Chiral Lipid Phases for Passive RNA Capture
abstract: Sealed lipid vesicles provide useful models for compartmentalization, but their bilayer boundaries limit post-assembly uptake of hydrated macromolecules such as RNA. Here, we demonstrate that short-chain monoacylglycerides form assemblies that take up RNA. Glycerol monodecanoate (GMD) and glycerol monononanoate (GMN) spontaneously organize in water into sponge phases (L3) with interconnected aqueous channels.

title: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Factors Governing CO Electro-Oxidation Pathways at Low Potentials on Platinum Single Crystal Electrodes
abstract: CO electro-oxidation on Pt is often interpreted primarily in terms of surface structure and CO coverage, yet the origin of the electro-oxidation processes preceding the main stripping peak remains unresolved. Here, we show that CO pre-oxidation is governed by the coupled effects of Pt surface structure, CO adlayer preparation, and the evolving electrostatic state of the Pt/CO-electrolyte interface.

title: Molecular Design of Non-Fluorinated Aryl-Extended Carbazole-Based Polymeric Membranes for Anion Exchange and Bipolar Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: The development of durable anion-exchange membranes (AEMs) that combine rapid hydroxide transport with restrained hydration and dimensional stability remains a central challenge for alkaline electrochemical technologies. Here, we synthesize a series of ether-free, arylexpanded carbazole-based AEMs bearing systematically varied N-alkyl substituents: N-ethyl (HCz-Et), N-butyl (HCz-Bu), and N-hexyl (HCz-Hex).

title: TEBench: a source-labelled thermoelectric data collection with leakage-safe splits and baselines for machine learning
abstract: Machine-learning thermoelectric scores are difficult to compare when source provenance and split groups differ. TEBench organises Starrydata Experiment-labelled curves (30,530 samples, 1,648,315 points, 6,045 papers), a JARVIS-DFT extract (23,558 structures) and an audited bulk Bi2Te3 workbook (740 records, 151 DOIs) as separate domains. DFT and experiment are never pooled. Canonical composition keys, paper/family/formula grouping and an eight-paper own-data hold-out support leakage review. The original Bi2Te3 Seebeck random forest reaches test R2 = 0.935 but own-paper R2 = −1.21.

title: Aromaticity, Electron Delocalization and Pauli Repulsion Explain Singlet and Triplet Energies in π-Systems Containing the Amide Moiety
abstract: Aromaticity has proven an invaluable principle for designing molecular singlet-fission chromophores. However, to effectively leverage aromaticity as part of a series of rational design principles, it is important to understand the interplay between aromaticity, electron delocalization, and singlet and triplet state energies. Here we report a multi-dimensional analysis of the relationship between aromaticity, electron-delocalization, and singlet/triplet state energies in a series of 114 amide-containing π-conjugated fused-ring systems.

title: GauMon: A Standalone, Cycle-Resolved Monitor for Gaussian Electronic-Structure Calculations
abstract: Electronic structure calculations can produce large and complex log files. Information such as self-consistent field (SCF) convergence, geometry optimization, numerical algorithms, and irregular termination can be found throughout the calculation. GauMon ( https://github.com/devashishdas/GauMon ) is an open-source Python desktop GUI application that monitors Gaussian calculation logs in real-time or allows examination of an existing log file. The software parses log files incrementally to monitor the state of a calculation.

title: Quantifying the Effectiveness of Independent Manual-Valve Verification in Preventing Product-Transfer Risks: A Monte Carlo Process-Safety Assessment
abstract: Manual valve line-ups before product transfers rely on rounds, radio confirmation and checklists, none of which observes valve position independently. We ask when an additional layer of temporary clamp-on position sensors on existing manual valves reduces transfer risk, and when alarm fatigue, bypass, common-cause failures and incomplete coverage remove the benefit.

title: A Hidden Silver Oxide Layer Rewrites Molecular Fingerprinting in Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: Gold (Au) and silver (Ag) are considered as interchangeable plasmonic components based on the implicit assumption that freshly prepared Ag nanomaterials remain metallic. However, we show, using in-situ surfaceaccessible SERS, that a sub-nanometer AgOx layer forms ubiquitously and instantaneously on colloidal Ag nanoparticles, and that this layer fundamentally alters our picture of how molecules interact with silver surfaces.

title: FLASH radiotherapy drives intestinal regeneration via macrophage-derived WNT4 signaling and attenuated T-cell inflammation
abstract: Ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) reduces normal-tissue toxicity, yet how elevated dose rate improves tissue repair remains unclear. Here we combined whole-abdominal FLASH-RT and conventional radiotherapy (CONV-RT) in mice with single-cell transcriptomics, trajectory analysis, cell-cell communication inference, and in vivo perturbation experiments to define the intestinal repair ecosystem. Compared with CONV-RT, FLASH preserved Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells and Fabp1+ absorptive epithelial cells. Trajectory analysis showed that FLASH maintained stem-cell differentiation toward mature epithelial states enriched for fatty-acid metabolism. During a day-3 repair window, FLASH was accompanied by enrichment of Mrc1 macrophages, increased WNT4-associated signaling involving Fzd5Lrp5/6-expressing stem cells, and early transient {beta}-catenin activation. In vivo augmentation of Wnt4 signaling promoted crypt regeneration after CONV-RT. FLASH also reduced Tcf7 and Tbx21 CD4 T-cell populations and TNF- levels, consistent with attenuation of the pro-inflammatory CD4 T-cell response during intestinal recovery. Together, these findings indicate that FLASH-associated tissue sparing involves coordinated remodeling of regenerative and inflammatory immune states, suggesting that radiation dose rate influences not only initial tissue injury but also the immune microenvironment of subsequent recovery. Targeting this immune-stem cell crosstalk may provide a strategy to mimic FLASH-like radioprotection.

title: Neuroinflammation and Brain Network Remodeling in Alzheimer's Disease: Integrating DTI, fMRI, TSPO-PET, and Fluid Biomarkers
abstract: In Alzheimer's disease (AD), how neuroinflammation triggers white-matter injury and remodels functional networks remains a core unresolved question. This narrative review surveys research progress, technical approaches, and outstanding challenges of multimodal neuroimagingincluding diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), functional MRI (fMRI), translocator protein PET (TSPOPET), and fluid biomarkers-in elucidating neuroinflammation in AD.

title: By carefully arranging molecules, scientists can control how a material responds to light, heat and physical force
abstract: University of Missouri researchers have created a single solid material that responds differently depending on what it's exposed to. Shine light on it, and it changes from yellow to white, an indication of a chemical reaction. Heat it, and it undergoes a different chemical reaction. Scratch the surface, and it flashes blue.

title: Chiral magnon Kerr interaction from linear and nonlinear Meissner screening in ferromagnet--superconductor bilayers
abstract: Magnon Kerr interaction showing a dependence of magnon dispersion frequency on its population is a useful functionality for nonlinear and quantum magnonics; its strength and sign depend on magnetic anisotropy, bias, and mode geometry. We here propose to use a superconducting gate to tune the Kerr interaction of magnons in ferromagnetic insulators. Even when the superconductor responds linearly, the frequency shift induced by its reflected dipolar field depends on the longitudinal magnetization. The decrease of this magnetization with increasing precession amplitude therefore produces a Kerr contribution. We go beyond this linear Meissner-screening regime by showing that at finite excitation amplitude, the significant Meissner screening currents reduce the superfluid stiffness, thus enhancing the effective magnetic-field penetration and rendering the Meissner backaction amplitude dependent. This superflow-induced pair breaking adds a second Kerr contribution, controlled by the interfacial superflow relative to the nonlinear screening scale. For yttrium iron garnet gated by dirty niobium, we predict a significant renormalization of the Kerr effect by superconductors, with the resulting Kerr contribution strongly chiral in the Damon--Eshbach configuration. By showing that the linear and nonlinear Meissner screening to the Kerr interaction can be distinguished by varying temperature, our work establishes a route to directional control of magnon nonlinear interactions.

title: Design of Self-Folding Origami Architectures for Biomedical Implants: A Finite Element Simulation Framework
abstract: Minimally invasive brain implants require compact deployment geometries and controlled shape transformation for delivery through confined vessels. Origami-inspired structures enable large shape changes from compact to tailored deployed configurations, but implementation at microscale dimensions remains challenging, as conventional designs rely on predefined mountain and valley folds that become increasingly difficult to fabricate and assemble as unit-cell size is reduced to meet clinical requirements. To address this, we propose a self-folding methodology based on thermally induced stresses in thin-film bimetallic composites. Pairing the shape memory alloy Nitinol (NiTi) with molybdenum or stainless steel (SS316L) exploits their differing thermal expansion coefficients to generate localized hinge bending, enabling deterministic, autonomous folding into prescribed mountain and valley configurations. Using finite element simulations, we systematically optimize hinge length, layer thickness, width, and shape, identifying a hinge geometry achieving a ~50% reduction in unit-cell dimensions relative to previously reported designs. Integration into a complete waterbomb origami unit cell confirms that the strip-level folding mechanism scales to produce coordinated, self-folding deformation across the tessellated structure. These results demonstrate the feasibility of stress-induced, self-folding thin-film origami architectures built from clinically established biomaterials, providing a scalable design framework for next-generation, active neurovascular implants with integrated sensing and monitoring functionality.

title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Aware Framework for Trustworthy Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Molecular property prediction is fundamental to computational chemistry and drug formulation research, yet existing benchmarks remain fragmented across datasets, properties, and evaluation protocols, limiting systematic evaluation of model generalization. We introduce Chem World, a large-scale benchmark integrating 17 public datasets with over 800,000 molecular and chemical-system instances across 10 property tracks, covering single-molecule and multi-component systems, including drug solubility. Chem World provides a unified testbed for evaluating molecular representations and compositional modeling across diverse chemical properties. Building on the benchmark, we propose PACM (Physics-Aware Compositional Modeling), which combines molecular representations with composition-aware modeling and domain-specific physical constraints. Extensive experiments show that molecular language models provide strong and transferable representations, while PACM consistently improves prediction across diverse chemical systems. Chem World and our PACM-powered drug-property prediction Agent support generalizable chemical modeling and offer a foundation for AI-assisted biomedical research and drug formulation development.

title: Design of Enhanced Multicomponent Gas Sensor Based on Neural Network Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation Algorithm
abstract: To satisfy the demand for high-precision online monitoring of early signature gases, carbon dioxide (CO2) and carbon monoxide (CO), in lithium-ion battery thermal runaway, we propose a multi-component gas sensing system based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) via Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation (CAKD). Prior knowledge learned by the teacher model from noisy second harmonic (2ƒ) signals is distilled into a structurally simpler student model, reducing inference latency and computational burden.

title: An opinion on machine learning for predicting nanoparticles
abstract: Multielement nanoparticles (ME-NPs), composed of five or more elements in roughly equal proportions, exhibit excellent inherent structural, compositional, and site-level diversity alongside exceptional thermal and physical properties, making them promising candidates for catalyst applications. However, traditional experimental methods rely heavily on trial-and-error processes that are time-consuming, inefficient, and cost-prohibitive. Machine learning (ML)/deep learning (DL) have emerged as powerful approaches to address these limitations by enabling scalable mapping between composition, site environment, or structure and ME-NP properties, and by facilitating the design of ME-NPs with targeted functionalities. This work presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art ML/DL applications for ME-NPs, covering key algorithms, databases, and evaluation metrics. Special emphasis is placed on property prediction, composition optimization, and phase identification, as well as emerging deep learning techniques. By estimating existing approaches and identifying emerging trends, this review provides a foundation for accelerating the characterization, optimization, and design of ME-NPs.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Programming Oxygen Reduction Selectivity via Peroxo Basicity: Acid-Controlled 2e–/4e– Reduction Switching at a Dicobalt Platform
abstract: Achieving switchable 2e–/4e– oxygen reduction selectivity within a single molecular catalyst remains an unmet challenge because the key metal–oxygen intermediate typically commits to one pathway. Herein, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome by elevating the basicity of the peroxo intermediate to a level where both proton-transfer (PT) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) manifolds become accessible, with the dominant pathway dictated solely by the external acid strength.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Elastic Landau states as martensite nuclei in austenite
abstract: In this article, we investigate the geometric closure of austenite--martensite interfaces. Classical compatibility conditions permit stress-free interfaces between the two phases: the condition $λ_2 = 1$ admits planar interfaces, whereas the cofactor conditions additionally admit curved interfaces. However, neither, guarantees the geometric closure of these interfaces. We identify two-parameter families of martensitic deformations that overcome this limitation and enable the formation of closed, stress-free martensite nuclei embedded in an austenite matrix. A main result is the interpretation of the classical deformation modes of simple shear and pure shear as martensitic phase transformations. These correspond to cubic to monoclinic-II and cubic to orthorhombic transformations, respectively. The former naturally satisfies the \emph{extreme compatibility conditions}, which are stronger than the cofactor conditions, and gives rise to \emph{elastic Landau states}, a self-accommodating martensitic nuclei embedded in austenite. We show that these states can be assembled to form arbitrarily shaped, stress-free martensitic islands surrounded by austenite. Such states can arise even in conventional shape memory alloys that do not satisfy supercompatibility, provided hierarchical twinning produces an average deformation that is a simple shear. The theory provides a geometric mechanism for self-accommodation. Its predicted deformation gradients agree with those reconstructed from experimentally observed microstructures. This agreement suggests that these microstructures originate from simple shear.

title: Structural and electronic properties of (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ phases from first principles
abstract: (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ material system is promising for ferroelectric devices, owing to their compatibility with the existing electronics manufacturing processes. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations can be used for the device design and optimization, but the predictive power of TCAD device simulations depends on the quality of the material parameters. These are still surprisingly poorly understood, also for the metastable ferroelectric phase, largely owing to the difficulties in synthesizing phase-pure samples. Here, we carry out high-quality first-principles calculations to extract reliable lattice parameters, dielectric constants, and band gaps for six of the most common phases of HfO$_2$, Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$, and ZrO$_2$. We compare results from GGA, meta-GGA, and hybrid functionals to shed light on the sensitivity of the results on the level of theory and to connect the results to earlier literature. In the case of band structures, we also consider $GW$ corrections as well as the effects of temperature-induced band gap renormalization and excitonic effects. Finally, we use these results in TCAD simulations for (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ FeCAP to demonstrate the effect that non-ferroelectric interlayers could have on the hysteresis curves and band diagrams.

title: JAX-WAVE: A Differentiable Physics-Supervised Framework for Inverse Wave Design in Heterogeneous Media
abstract: Designing a prescribed wave field in a heterogeneous medium requires an initial pressure distribution that compensates for the medium's propagation response. Repeated numerical inversion solves this task afresh for each target and environment. We introduce JAX-WAVE for amortized inverse wave design: a shared neural network maps desired terminal fields and known wave-speed maps directly to bounded initial pressures. Training through a differentiable finite-difference time-domain solver uses the physical design objective without requiring optimized control labels. Linear propagation and symmetric pressure bounds imply an exact sign-reversal relation for the regularized optimum. A shared-weight projection enforces this relation, preserves feasibility, and satisfies an exact identity for the paired-sign objective. We characterize the discrete propagator and its weighted adjoint to connect learning, numerical inversion, and optimality assessment. On an independent confirmation set, three trained models achieve unseen-material errors of 25.24% for geometric targets and 4.77% for reachable targets. Matched-capacity comparisons show improved reconstruction with the sign parameterization. Within a 5 ms median online budget, the learned map reduces mean error by 45% relative to accelerated numerical inversion on the heterogeneous benchmark; longer numerical solves recover greater accuracy. The results establish a reusable inverse-design procedure and show how its accuracy and computational value depend on target structure and query workload.

title: Orchestr.AI: A Unified Workflow for Training and Benchmarking of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine-learning force fields enable atomistic simulations at near-reference accuracy and substantially reduced computational cost, but their development remains fragmented across software frameworks with incompatible data formats, configuration schemes, dependencies, and execution procedures. Orchestr.AI addresses this limitation through a unified workflow that coordinates different MLIP software frameworks, referred to as engines, for data preparation, model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and deployment. A common YAML interface defines each experiment, while engine-specific environment profiles preserve compatible software stacks and avoid dependency conflicts. The platform currently supports five MLIP model architectures, namely SchNet, PaiNN, NequIP, Allegro, and MACE, through their corresponding software implementations, providing automated configuration mapping and standardized dataset handling across these frameworks. Benchmarks on the rMD17 and 3BPA datasets show that Orchestr.AI reproduces the expected performance trends while enabling controlled cross-engine comparisons. Repeated executions with fixed configurations and engine profiles produce highly consistent results, demonstrating practical workflow reproducibility. Beyond training, Orchestr.AI provides modular architectural interfaces that connect trained models to ASE-based simulations, batch inference, epistemic uncertainty estimation, calibration, and active-learning workflows. The platform therefore provides a reproducible and extensible infrastructure for developing, comparing, and deploying machine-learning interatomic potentials, which we validate here through cross-engine accuracy and repeatability benchmarks.

title: Large-Scale and Systematic Prediction of ADMET Properties through Heterogeneous Network and Kernel-Based Deep Learning
abstract: Accurately predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties remains a major challenge in accelerating drug discovery, especially for underexplored natural products (NPs). Herein, we present a unified multitask learning framework that integrated heterogeneous network (HN) embeddings and a modified kernel-based deep neural network (DNN) to simultaneously predict all ADMET properties.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Landfill leachate tests reveal divergent fates of biodegradable plastics
abstract: Even among plastics labeled "biodegradable," some break down readily while others persist for long periods. In experiments using landfill leachate, a collaborative research team led by the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) demonstrated these differences and identified candidate microorganisms and enzymes potentially involved in plastic degradation.

title: Programming golden triple helices
abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

title: Electronic Origin of Contrasting Li and Na Clustering on Graphene
abstract: The electrochemical performance of anode materials is often defined by the ability of metal ions (e.g., Li and Na) to be effectively stored within the host material over a specific range of chemical potentials. This is particularly true for adsorbed Li and Na atoms on carbon surfaces (e.g., graphite or pore surfaces in hard carbon), where the interplay between ionic and metallic bonding often takes place - while metal atoms act as ionic species, in a finite concentration limit, they tend to form metallic bonding when they approach each other. What makes the case special is that, despite similar chemical identities, Li and Na atoms exhibit distinct tendencies for cluster formation; for example, the formation of Li metallic clusters on a graphene surface is only thermodynamically favorable after reaching a finite metal-ion concentration. Motivated by this, herein, we use first-principles calculations on graphene to examine the electronic origin of Li and Na clustering. Specifically, we demonstrate that the separated adsorbed atoms donate electrons to graphene, shifting the Fermi level to higher energies; however, the formation of metal clusters can result in the formation of lower-energy orbitals that are specifically associated with metal-metal bonding, thus lowering the Fermi level (and hence total energies). Importantly, while the process is somewhat similar for Na and Li atoms, the energy levels of the newly formed metallic states govern the difference in metallic cluster formation between Li and Na.

title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones
abstract: Existing sequential user modeling methods mainly focus on improving the backbone encoder or learning task-specific user representations for a single prediction objective. We instead study how to export the multi-layer user states of a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream training backfill and serving. In this setting, the user state at a given timestamp summarizes the user's actions before that time, so downstream systems need only the state aligned to each target timestamp rather than the full hidden-state timeline. To this end, we present \texttt{SeqFold}, a compressed-state interface that combines learned multi-channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay, and Lookup-Free Quantization (LFQ) to produce compact discrete codes from frozen backbone states. Task-specific decoders then map these shared codes into flexible embedding spaces for downstream models. To make timestamp-addressable export practical at scale, we further develop a fused streaming implementation that updates the fusion recurrence after every action while materializing states only at target timestamps. On large-scale proprietary datasets, SeqFold reduces per-state representation storage by $3{,}400\times$ while preserving most of the downstream ranking performance of the uncompressed model, showing that SeqFold is an effective interface for reusing long-history sequence backbones in downstream models.

title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
abstract: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
abstract: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to Sn(OH)$_3$-Me and its hydrates, minimal models of organotin photoresists for extreme-ultraviolet lithography, from 32 to 70 qubits. After one round of hardware sampling, followed by classical ranking and recovery of the cached counts with the molecular Hamiltonian and no further QPU calls, 27 of 28 runs at 46-70 qubits are within 15 mHa of the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) reference (median 4.5 mHa), and in all eight runs with an untrained control the trained policy is more accurate. At 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use 34-72 times fewer two-qubit gates than the local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuit transpiled for the same device. These results demonstrate that circuit generators can be trained with quantum hardware at 70 qubits.

title: Beyond Interaction Scores: Selecting Feature Interactions via Independent Replication
abstract: Learning feature interactions is essential for accurate prediction and interpretable modeling, yet a high interaction score may reflect fitting noise rather than a reproducible pattern. Ranking methods score feature pairs but leave the cutoff to the user; testing methods set the cutoff but rely on repeated model refits or a model of the joint feature distribution. We present LENS, a model-agnostic framework for selecting feature interactions through independent replication. LENS trains two models with the same learning algorithm on disjoint data and accesses them only through predictions. For each feature pair, it removes main effects from the joint-effect surface to isolate an interaction pattern, ranks pairs by its strength, and tests whether the second model reproduces it at a meaningful strength. A single multiple-testing correction determines which pairs to retain, using only two model fits regardless of the number of features. We prove that a replication ratio alone can retain arbitrarily weak patterns shared by both fits, whereas a strength floor restores selection consistency, and we characterize when normalization in Friedman's $H^2$ reverses interaction rankings. On 16 synthetic designs, LENS matches leading model-specific ranking methods (e.g., TreeSHAP) and recovers 91% of material interactions, against 45% for the knockoff-based DIAMOND, without selecting false pairs; with 1,225 candidate pairs and no interactions, it makes substantially fewer false discoveries. On large-scale French motor insurance data, it identifies interactions documented in the actuarial literature and recovers 90% of the deviance gain obtained using all pairs. On two credit datasets, LENS selects few pairs while maintaining or slightly improving predictive performance over the additive baseline.

title: Global fossil fuel emissions set to fall in 2026, but total CO2 keeps rising
abstract: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground, but rising emissions from deforestation threaten to push total CO2 emissions to a new record. Scientists warn that the world's remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C could be exhausted in less than four years, even as a lasting decline in emissions appears increasingly within reach.
